text: Could we talk about it on Thursday?
We could move one field team from the north to the south.
Coverage in the south might go up by three points.
The north might not stay ahead of plan without that team.
You asked for options, so here are two.
We could move one team, or we could hire a new one.
The downside is that the north might fall behind.
I would suggest option one as a pilot for one quarter.

When a director comes into my office and says we must do this, my first reaction is to look for the problem with it. I cannot help it. Must is a closed door, and people want to open closed doors. When the same director says we could do this, and here is what it might cost us, my reaction is completely different. I start thinking about how to make it work, because the idea is still open and I am part of it. So my advice to anyone with a proposal is simple. Bring two options, not one. Say what each one could do and what might go wrong. Then say which one you would suggest, and why. You will get more yes answers with could and might than you ever got with must, and the strange thing is that people will think you are more confident, not less.

There is a difference between could and might that a lot of people miss, even native speakers. Could is about what is possible. It opens a door. We could move a team, we could hire, we could wait. Might is about what is uncertain. It warns you about the other side of the door. Coverage might go up. The north might fall behind. Hiring might take two months. In a good proposal you need both. Could gives the room options, and might shows the room that you have already thought about the risk. And one more thing about the end of a proposal. Do not finish with a statement. Finish with a question, like could we talk about it on Thursday, or might this work for your team. A question at the end gives the decision back to the room, and a room that decides is a room that supports you.
We could hire a second field team for the south.
The north might fall behind without that team.
The campaign might not be ready before the trade fair.
We could wait until next year.
Could we talk about it on Thursday?
You asked for options, so here are two.
We could move one team, or we could hire a new one.
The downside is that the north might fall behind.
I would suggest option one as a pilot for one quarter.
